name: VIctory
approach: A Rust layer that loads the Xbox executable into its own process and runs the code unchanged. It stands in for the console’s system services and Direct3D, and recompiles the console’s GPU programs to DXIL. Most builds that play the game are forks of it.

fps.text: about 1 fps in the world, 30 in menus

hardware: Radeon RX 6700 XT 12 GB, Windows 11
missing: Ray-traced shadows and bounce light never run
Fewer than 300 of 24,387 shader programs do not translate, and their draws are dropped
HDR and the game’s own upscaler
Offline only by design; speech and reverb are silent

name: VIctory-RDNA
approach: A fork of the 7900 XTX build tuned for AMD RDNA3 cards. It maps the game’s buffers in place and keeps large ones in video memory to cut the copying that slows other forks.

fps.text: 20.8 fps median over a 24 minute run at 4K, 23.1 in a shorter one

hardware: Radeon RX 7900 XT 20 GB, Series X profile at 4K output
target: A stable 30 fps or more without ray tracing
missing: Ray tracing is off
Needs 32 GB of RAM, with 64 GB recommended
Measured on one PC, with no test from outside the project

name: VIctory-7900XTX
approach: AvatarManz’s fork patches the game’s renderer so it behaves like a PC renderer and translates shaders ahead of time into a store kept between builds. It merges work from victory-fork, DexNom and Belobug.

fps.text: 23 fps walking at 1080p output, 16 at 4K and 9 with ray tracing on

hardware: Radeon RX 7900 XTX, Core i9-12900K, 64 GB RAM
target: The Series X version at 4K with ray tracing, then 30 fps or more
missing: Models and textures stay at low detail for a long time while the game streams them
Ray-traced structures of moving objects are partly corrupt
Uses 37 to 45 GB of RAM

name: VIctory-Belobug-AMD
approach: Belobug’s AMD fork follows VIctory’s main branch and adds a stand-in for the game’s ray-traced bounce light. PortWatch reports having seen it play through missions with a picture close to the console’s.

fps.text: about 22 fps in a city street with ray tracing off

hardware: Radeon RX 7900 XTX, Series S profile (the README shares its measurements with the 7900 XTX fork)
target: A stable 30 fps or more without ray tracing
missing: Trees, signs and far objects flicker in places
Lighting is too bright or too dark for a while after walking indoors
Textures appear late
About 30 GB of RAM in use, 64 GB recommended

name: Vice-Tay
approach: A VIctory tree tuned on one RTX 4090 PC. Every change is checked in CI and then in a recorded play session with frame rate and memory read from the game’s own frame lines.

fps.text: 21.1 fps median over a 30 minute session

hardware: GeForce RTX 4090, Ryzen 9 9950X3D, 48 GB RAM, Series S profile
target: The open world at 30 fps with a correct picture
missing: Short of 30 fps
Measured on the Series S profile only
Frame rate eased and memory grew by about 1 GB over the session
No test from outside the project

name: VIctory on NVIDIA
approach: A fork for NVIDIA cards that swaps the game’s upscaler for DLSS and adds frame generation. On 26 November it moved onto foxhound, which took the same rooms from 15 to 17 fps to 26 to 30 at a higher resolution.

fps.text: 26 to 30 fps in the opening rooms, 30 on the first boat ride

hardware: GeForce RTX 5070 12 GB, Ryzen 7 9800X3D, 64 GB RAM, Series X profile at 1440p with DLSS Quality
missing: No ray tracing
Frame generation needs spare video memory
Stutter on a first run while shaders compile

name: AnyXboxX
approach: Began as an emulator that interpreted the console runtime on Unicorn. Its GTA VI results now come from a bundled copy of VIctory that builds on Vice-Tay, and its launcher plays at 1080p by default.

fps.text: about 24 fps median in the world at 1080p over a 14 minute session, about 20 at 4K

hardware: GeForce RTX 4070 SUPER, Core i7-13700KF, Series X mode
missing: Ray tracing is off, so interiors and shadows are dark
Some graphics are missing
Uses 20 to 25 GB of RAM

name: KLBF Lab
approach: Combines fixes from several VIctory forks into one tested build, with its own AMD stability work, water physics and optional FSR frame generation. It also proposes a shared way to measure frame rate.

fps.text: 18.5 fps average on the Series S profile with FSR 4, 16.9 over an hour on Series X

hardware: Radeon RX 9070 XT 16 GB, Ryzen 7 9800X3D, 32 GB RAM, Series S profile with FSR 4
missing: An outside tester’s five minute benchmark averaged 8.3 fps on an RTX 4070
Linux support is community work in progress
note: An unreleased build averaged 21.8 fps over an hour with scripted input.

name: VI-BR-PORT
approach: A Brazilian fork aimed at 8 GB NVIDIA cards and a 1080p monitor. It skips the ray-tracing skinning pass and swaps bounce light for a constant ambient term.

fps.text: 26.6 to 27.9 fps walking in the prison, 28.7 to 29.1 on the first boat ride

hardware: GeForce RTX 4060 Ti 8 GB, Core i7-13700K, 64 GB RAM, Series S profile at 1080p
target: A steady 30 fps from the opening to the boat ride
missing: Heavy stretches of the prison and the opening fall to 18 to 24 fps
Night scenes are darker than on console, and walls vanish in an occasional frame
No run longer than 12 minutes has been measured
No ray-traced lighting

name: Kelvaroq
approach: A Rust runtime built on VIctory and victory-fork by a French studio. It replaces the per-frame memory bookkeeping that it measured as the main cost in other forks.

fps.text: about 10 fps in the prologue, 7 to 8 in its heaviest scenes

hardware: GeForce RTX 5080 at 3840×2160
target: 3840×2160 at 30 fps with steady frame pacing
missing: Some shader pipelines are missing and some draws are dropped
Video memory pressure
One outside playtest so far: 36 minutes on an RTX 4090, up to the first mission

name: victory-fork
approach: hyphennn’s fork, formerly victory-gta6. It follows VIctory’s main branch and adds rendering and speed fixes, with autosaves and checkpoints working. Several other forks build on it.

fps.text: about 11 fps at the first boat mission; 0.2 to 3 with ray-traced shadows on

hardware: GeForce RTX 4070 12 GB, Core i7-14700KF, 32 GB RAM, Series X profile
missing: Anything the sun does not hit directly is black, because ray-traced bounce light and shadows do not run
The graphics card is lost 30 to 50 minutes into a session
Uses 23 to 27 GB of RAM

name: VIctory NVIDIA 8 GB
approach: A fork of victory-fork for 8 GB GeForce cards. Dropping two texture mip levels keeps the card from running out of memory.

fps.text: 8 to 10 fps at 1080p, 6 at native 4K

hardware: GeForce RTX 4060 Laptop 8 GB, Core i5-12450H, 48 GB RAM, Series X profile
missing: Lower texture detail to fit 8 GB
Tested on one laptop

name: VItoriaBr
approach: Uilian’s fork merges victory-fork’s world rendering with his own NVIDIA work and is developed on live streams. It finishes the prologue and reaches the first story mission.

fps.text: 4 to 6 fps on the default preset; 22 in one experimental build

hardware: GeForce RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB, Ryzen 7 5700X, 40 GB RAM
missing: Progress stops at the first story mission
Occasional crashes entering the world and in some scenes
The 22 fps build is not merged

name: Leonida Legacy
approach: Keeps the Leonida name but is a fork of victory-fork. It picks settings for the player’s graphics card and ships scripts so testers without programming experience can send measurements.

fps.text: 2 to 4 fps in the world, about 10 in the first rooms with newer switches

hardware: GeForce RTX 3080 12 GB, Ryzen 7 7800X3D, 32 GB RAM (frame rates measured upstream on an RTX 4070)
missing: Shadowed areas are black
Frame rates not yet measured on its own test PC

name: ScarlettPort
approach: A runtime forked from the VIctory line with its own launcher. Version 0.4.6 rebuilt the renderer for lit rooms and complete textures without ray tracing, and 0.5 about doubled its frame rate.

fps.text: about 7 to 8 fps in the world on its own RTX 3060; a tester’s Radeon RX 9060 XT reports a 22 fps median

hardware: GeForce RTX 3060 12 GB, Ryzen 5 5600X, Series S profile
missing: Playable speed: most NVIDIA cards report under 10 fps
Haze indoors
The ray-tracing structure builder makes stray writes

name: victory-amd
approach: An AMD fork of victory-fork that measures what each frame is made of. JoshuuDev’s copy of it is the base of the private Doomsday build.

fps.text: 2.5 to 4 fps, 9.6 in the first rooms with newer switches

hardware: One PC with 32 GB RAM, Series X profile
missing: Shadowed areas are black
Its README says it is not playable yet

name: DexNom RayTime
approach: An AMD fork that keeps the game’s ray tracing on. The game builds and walks its ray-tracing structures through translated Direct3D 12 compute shaders, with FSR 4.1.2 upscaling to 4K.

fps.text: 1.1 to 1.3 fps with ray tracing on

hardware: Radeon RX 7900 XTX 24 GB
missing: Frame times can reach several seconds
Some materials still render black
Interior lighting and shadows vary by scene

name: XCL
approach: An independent Rust layer in the spirit of Wine. It runs Xbox code natively, writes its own versions of the console libraries and recompiles shaders through HLSL to DXIL. It lists GTA VI only as “a newer retail game”.

fps.text: about 5 fps in the 3D world, 30 in menus

hardware: GeForce RTX 5090, on an unmerged NVIDIA branch
missing: The world’s picture is incomplete: the minimap and other mesh pipelines are refused
It does not keep running in the world for long

name: Five Star Recomp
approach: A C# layer and toolkit written for GTA VI, with a translator that turns each console GPU program into HLSL.

fps.text: about one second a frame in the world; the opening cutscene’s cards and sound run at 30

missing: World surfaces are black while material textures are fixed
No capture published

name: PercyScarlett
approach: A Rust layer with stand-in system DLLs and its own shader recompiler. Version 1.0 reaches the opening prison scene, lit and textured, on an 8 GB card. It swaps the console build of FSR 4 for a plain stretch so the picture reaches the screen. Its README calls the game “TheBig6”.

fps.text: about 2 to 3 fps on the Series S profile, 1 on Series X

hardware: GeForce RTX 2060 SUPER 8 GB
missing: Shaded areas and interiors are too dark without ray-traced lighting
Speed

name: Scarlight
approach: A Steam compatibility tool for Linux that runs the Xbox build through Proton on Mesa drivers.

fps.text: 1.5 to 3 fps in a fixed scene, down to 0.1 in busy ones

hardware: Radeon RX 9070 XT, Mesa 26.3.1, CachyOS
missing: Its README says it is not playable
One game tested on one card

name: VIctory for macOS
approach: Runs VIctory on Apple Silicon through Wine and Apple’s D3DMetal. A student maintains it and credits Claude for much of the work.
hardware: M2 Max, 32 GB, CrossOver 26.3 with D3DMetal 4.0 beta 3
missing: Nobody has reached gameplay on a Mac
An M5 Pro presented 64 black frames and stopped
The furthest run depends on patches that are not merged

name: Native VIctory for macOS
approach: Ports VIctory to macOS without Wine. The game’s code runs in the port’s own process and shaders go through Apple’s Metal Shader Converter. A contributor’s branch recompiles the game’s 440,000 functions to arm64.

fps.text: 1 to 3 fps in the world, about 30 in menus

hardware: M5 Pro, 48 GB
missing: Most of the world’s surfaces are missing and nothing is lit
A world run can still end in a GPU time-out or a crash
Macs with 16 to 24 GB run short of GPU memory
The arm64 build is not on the main branch
note: The project rates itself about 55% done and says it cannot give a date.

name: TuxBox
approach: A Linux-first layer that adds the console-specific parts on top of Proton: the Xbox flavour of Direct3D 12, a shader translator and the memory, input and storage calls games use. Windows has a native Direct3D 12 backend.
hardware: GeForce RTX 4070 Ti SUPER
missing: GTA VI reaches the prologue cutscene on Linux and runs out of memory there
No retail game is playable yet

name: XValkyrie
approach: A C++ layer for Xbox One and Series games that runs code natively and turns shaders into HLSL. It publishes a compatibility list of every title it has tried, with Fortnite, Unicorn Overlord and Minecraft Preview among the Series ones.
missing: No GTA VI result published

name: Xbox Emulator
approach: Continues the TomBox project: a Rust runtime that runs decrypted Xbox Series builds as ordinary Windows processes. It reports Trackmania driving at about 60 fps and Fortnite reaching its lobby.
missing: No GTA VI result in the public repository
The developer’s GTA VI work is private and shown on streams

name: Leonida
approach: The first and largest project. It translated all 26,503 console shaders to SPIR-V for Vulkan and built a loader and import shims, with the aim of producing a native Windows program from the user’s files.
missing: Never showed a frame of the retail game
note: The Discord server of about 180,000 members was removed on 23 November and the 15-year-old lead quit that night. GitHub processed Take-Two’s notice on 24 November and disabled the repository with a network of 3,007 repositories.

name: Leonida Continued
approach: The largest continuation of Leonida’s code. It keeps the Vulkan path, with all 26,503 shaders translated to SPIR-V, and builds ray-tracing structures in the console’s own layout.
missing: Nothing is playable
It runs the story load to the end, and no world frame has been verified
Ray tracing is in progress

name: Leonida CE
approach: A community edition of Leonida that keeps its history and license. The game’s own interface appears and walks through first-boot setup.
missing: The graphics device is lost about two minutes after the legal terms
Some streamed texture formats cannot be decoded yet

name: Palmetto
approach: Translates the console executable and shaders at build time and runs them on a Direct3D 12 device backed by Vulkan. It began as a continuation of Leonida.
hardware: GeForce RTX 4090, Core i9-13900K
missing: Every presented frame reads back black
Measured on one PC

name: Project ReCity
approach: A static recompilation of version 1.0.2.1 into a native Windows program with a Vulkan renderer. Its shader translator has been tested on more than 30 GPU and driver combinations.
missing: The game does not boot
The loader has only run a test executable

name: Xbox2Windows
approach: Research into translating Xbox Series machine code to C++ and its shaders to DXIL, with public tests that run without a game.
hardware: GeForce RTX 4060 Laptop
missing: Only a modified diagnostic executable has played the intro and reached loading
851 of 12,101 pixel shaders are verified
Menus and gameplay are unverified

name: ScarlettX
approach: A clean-room high-level emulator of the Xbox Series operating system, game runtime and Direct3D. It runs a small retail game, Concept Destruction, at about 188 fps.
missing: No GTA VI work
Shader lifting for retail games and the console’s shared memory are not started
No commits since 22 November

name: XSXEmu
approach: An emulator for Apple Silicon that runs the game’s x86-64 code through Rosetta and translates shaders to Metal without Wine.
hardware: Apple M4
missing: GTA VI starts worker threads and reads its archives, and has not produced a frame
0 of 28,164 shipped pipelines are ready

name: KytyPS5
approach: A translation layer for PS5 games on Windows and Linux, with experimental macOS support. It loads the game’s executable and maps PS5 system calls and graphics to the host. A community thread tracks the games it needs to run before GTA VI: GTA V is in game at about 56 fps on an RTX 5060 and Cyberpunk 2077 at about 14.
hardware: Users’ PCs on Windows and Linux, from a Radeon RX 6600 to a GeForce RTX 5090
missing: Crashes as the world starts to load: one user traced it to the game’s own watchdog firing while very large compute shaders compile
No picture past the setup screens and start menu
Asset streaming and performance for a game this size
note: The GTA VI results are users’ reports in the project’s issue tracker from 26 and 27 November. The maintainers have not posted one.

name: AnyPS5
approach: Converts a PS5 executable into a native Windows or Linux program and links it against its own versions of the PS5 system libraries, with a shader recompiler that outputs SPIR-V. No emulator or separate runtime runs beside the game.
hardware: A tester’s PC: Ryzen 9 9950X3D, GeForce RTX 3090
missing: The screen stays black
Frames stop after about 100 seconds and the game’s own watchdog ends the run
No menus or gameplay
note: The GTA VI result comes from testers in the project’s discussions, using changes that are not merged. The maintainers have not posted one.

name: GTA VI Translation Layer
approach: Adds GTA VI research, patches and progress tracking on top of AnyPS5. The project refuses to work from leaked files.
missing: Nothing has been tested with GTA VI
15 of 138 roadmap tasks cannot start until the game’s files can be studied lawfully

name: CGBJ
approach: A private build that combines VIctory and XCL. Its code went public under the GPL on 26 November and was unreachable within two hours. Open forks such as foxhound carry copies of it on.

fps.text: 25 fps average

missing: No public code from its owner
The 25 fps figure is relayed by PortWatch with no card, scene or run length
Its own development journal showed 17 to 18 fps on an RTX 5090

name: darkworldhm
approach: A private build shown on a stream on 25 November in free roam on an NVIDIA card.

fps.text: 12 to 15 fps in free roam, swinging between 5 and 24

missing: No public code
Its base is not known

name: NotNozy
approach: A private build on an AMD card, shown on a stream, that looks close to the 7900 XTX fork.

fps.text: about 16 fps

missing: No public code
Its base is not known

name: Doomsday
approach: A private group’s build on JoshuuDev’s victory-amd fork, with ray-traced lighting running.

fps.text: 3 to 5 fps with ray-traced lighting

missing: No public code

name: suri
approach: A private build on victory-fork. PortWatch confirmed a player moving through Lucia’s prologue.

fps.text: about 3 fps

missing: No public code

name: omonkey
approach: The Xbox Emulator developer’s private GTA VI work, streamed live. A player walks slowly around the opening prison scene.

fps.text: about 5 fps in the prison scene

missing: No public code

name: ZETTROX
approach: A build of VIctory and victory-fork for NVIDIA cards. It played from Lucia’s prologue into Jason’s first mission and led PortWatch’s ranking on 25 November.

fps.text: about 2 fps

missing: Anything in shadow rendered black
note: The repository and the owner’s account returned 404 on 26 November. GitHub has published no notice for it.

name: americas-recomp
approach: A fork of AnyPS5 that tested whether the PS5 tool’s shader recompiler could handle the Xbox game.
missing: Did not boot the game
note: PortWatch dates the removal to 23 November. The owner’s account is still active and no notice is published.

name: keylime
approach: A C++20 runtime written from scratch with Vulkan graphics and its own shader translator. It reported the intro and main menu at 30 fps.
missing: The opening cutscene did not draw
note: The repository returned 404 on 26 November. No notice is published.

name: foxhound
approach: A VIctory fork tuned for GeForce RTX cards. It hands the game’s upscaling to DLSS, runs the Series X profile at 1440p and cuts stalls. It was taken from the code CGBJ published briefly, and VIctory-NVIDIA now builds on it.

fps.text: about 29 fps over a 7 minute run of the opening, holding the game’s 30 fps cap on the first boat ride

hardware: GeForce RTX 4070 SUPER 12 GB, Ryzen 7 7800X3D, 32 GB RAM, Series X profile at 1440p with DLSS Quality
missing: Nothing after the first boat ride has been tested
No ray tracing: an estimate stands in for bounce light and reflections
Hitches while a new scene streams in
Testers with slower processors report 10 to 15 fps
note: The figures come from one run on the author’s PC.

name: Vilocity
approach: A Rust layer for Xbox Series games on Windows with its own launcher. Its engine comes from the VIctory line by way of CGBJ’s code, with fixes ported from other forks.

fps.text: 26 to 27 fps in lighter scenes and 17 to 19 in the heaviest; one unattended 12 minute run of the opening had a 33 fps median

hardware: GeForce RTX 5080, Ryzen 9 9950X3D, 62 GB RAM, Series S profile at 1080p
missing: Its README says it is not playable yet
No mission has been played start to finish
A driver timeout about 7 minutes into some runs
Draws from 26 console programs are dropped on 32-lane cards
Shade is too dark in daylight
